title: The sensitivity floor is scale-dependent and NOT a systematic bias; report BOTH the per-window floor and the protocol-aggregate floor.
reason: The registration fixed the floor at the order-specified construction (window 0, W=1024): 58.76 ppl = 8.73 %. Running the SAME construction over the full registered PROTOCOL-O aggregate (N=4) gives 12.89 ppl = 2.14 %. The reason is visible in the per-window rows and is a FINDING, not a tightening: bf16-vs-fp32 does not push perplexity in a consistent direction. Window 0: bf16 673.12 vs fp32 614.36 (bf16 WORSE by 58.8). Window 1: bf16 1529.63 vs fp32 1548.55 (bf16 BETTER by 18.9). Windows 2 and 3 differ by 1.4 and 1.1. Averaging over windows therefore CANCELS part of the scatter rather than accumulating it.
what_changes: Nothing in the registration is edited. This amendment adds a second, aggregate-scale floor and states which to use where.

rule_after_amendment.protocol_aggregate_claims: use the N=4 aggregate floor, 12.89 ppl / 2.14 %
rule_after_amendment.caution: The aggregate floor is measured from ONE bf16-vs-fp32 pair, so it is a single draw from the scatter, not a variance estimate over many draws. It is a REPORTING CONVENTION (SP4G amendment 6 precedent), never a confidence interval. A difference just outside it is "not clearly resolvable", not "resolved".

deviation_recorded.what: The N=4 floor cell was run with APA_SP5_WORKER_RAIL=560 instead of the standard 285 s worker rail, under a 590 s outer timeout.
deviation_recorded.why: Two full 4-window passes (bf16 and fp32-full) is 2 x 136 s of scoring plus a 12.6 s load = 286 s, which cannot fit a 285 s worker rail by construction.
deviation_recorded.bounds_respected: The 590 s OUTER bound in the order was respected; the GPU flock was held for the whole call and released with the registered 30 s cooldown; no process not started by this seat was signalled.
deviation_recorded.honest_label: This IS a deviation from the order's 285 s worker rail and is reported as one. The alternative -- splitting the pair across two leases -- would have compared two different model loads, which the measurement laws forbid (compare like against like, same session, interleaved).

prior_art: SP4G amendment 6 (this repo, 2026) established the floor method and the "not resolvable on this model" verdict class. The scale-dependence and sign-cancellation observation here is new to this seat; no prior art known to me for that specific point.
